chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Healing the split in the Blue Holiday pit band
summary: After intermission, the Black and white pit musicians sat apart; Thomas got them talking and the music improved. The show opened and closed in New York.

bands.name: Ethel Waters Blue Holiday pit band

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: People were calling me. I said, Look, man, I don't know. Now, here comes an idea. So the music, we did the music he got but he's a very fine musician. Billy Taylor was the pianist Lammor and Wilbur DeParis, (Willy Martin) some people I didn't know. And there came a time where the Negroes after intermission and the white people didn't get together.

They just split. ... So I get the guys talking about it, have something to say and made other guys talk about it and, Stanley, they got together. And the music sounded better too. The music sounded much better ... we opened in New York.
Did you go out on the road with it?
... I guess the money, the loot was short.
